reply.title: At the Highest Point of a Vertical Throw
reply.story:
When you toss a ball straight up into the air, it slows down as it climbs, stops for a fleeting instant at its highest point, and then speeds up on its way back down. Watching it pause at the top, it is easy to wonder if gravity takes a break too. Since its speed is zero at that exact peak, does its acceleration drop to zero as well?

To find out, we can track the ball's motion from the moment it leaves the hand until it falls back down. Even though the velocity changes continuously from positive to negative, the downward pull of gravity never stops acting on the ball.
reply.cardDescription: Explore what happens to velocity and acceleration when a ball is thrown straight up. See why the velocity is zero at the top while the acceleration remains constant at $-9.8 \text{ m/s}^2$.
reply.instructions: Adjust the launch speed and press Play to observe how velocity changes while acceleration stays constant.
